description: Missing comma in the SELECT column list, causing a syntax error in the query.
broken_query: SELECT id username email FROM users;
gold_query: SELECT id, username, email FROM users;
hints: Check the column list in the SELECT statement.
SQL requires a comma separating each selected column.

description: Incorrect use of WERE instead of WHERE, leading to invalid SQL syntax.
hints: Look closely at the filtering keyword used.
The keyword for condition filtering is WHERE.

description: Use of INNER JOIN incorrectly excludes required rows; should be replaced with LEFT JOIN.
broken_query: SELECT users.username, orders.id FROM users INNER JOIN orders ON users.id = orders.user_id;
gold_query: SELECT users.username, orders.id FROM users LEFT JOIN orders ON users.id = orders.user_id;
hints: What happens if a user doesn't have any orders?
Consider using an outer join to include all left-hand records regardless of a match.

description: Incorrect aggregation using COUNT(*) instead of SUM(total_amount), resulting in wrong output.
broken_query: SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) as total_spent FROM orders GROUP BY user_id;
gold_query: SELECT user_id, SUM(total_amount) as total_spent FROM orders GROUP BY user_id;
hints: Are you counting the number of rows, or summing up a specific value?
Replace the aggregation function with one that adds numeric values.

description: Correlated subquery runs multiple times (N+1 problem); needs optimization using JOIN and GROUP BY.
broken_query: SELECT id, name, (SELECT SUM(quantity) FROM order_items WHERE product_id = products.id) AS total_sold FROM products;
gold_query: SELECT products.id, products.name, COALESCE(SUM(order_items.quantity), 0) AS total_sold FROM products LEFT JOIN order_items ON products.id = order_items.product_id GROUP BY products.id, products.name;
hints: Avoid using subqueries in the SELECT clause when dealing with many rows.
Join the tables and use GROUP BY to perform the aggregation in a single query pass.
